# Use md-to-confluence

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Turn a Markdown runbook, design note or guide into a Confluence page: storage-format XHTML with real code blocks, tables, tasks, info and warning panels, images as attachments and an optional contents macro, a warning for everything dropped, and an optional publish that first shows which page it will create or overwrite and at what version, refuses stale or wrong-space overwrites, and takes credentials only from the environment.

**Reach for it when** the user says "put this in Confluence", "publish this markdown to the wiki", "update the Confluence page with this", "convert to Confluence storage format", or names a Confluence space for a Markdown file.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install md-to-confluence                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install md-to-confluence --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install md-to-confluence --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Converters pack: [`--pack converters`](../packs/use-the-converters-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/converters/skills/md-to-confluence/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "put this runbook in Confluence under the SRE space"
- "Convert README.md to Confluence storage format so I can paste it into the source editor"
- "Publish design-notes.md as a wiki page under Architecture on our atlassian site"
- "update Confluence page 48213 with the new deploy-checklist.md"
- "our team docs live in Confluence, can you get this markdown onto a page with the code blocks looking right"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Convert this markdown to a Word document legal can track changes in"
- "Turn the markdown report into a single HTML file I can email"
- "Create Jira epics and issues from this PRD"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use md-to-confluence".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **The right page, said out loud.** Every publish is preceded by the page id, title, space, current version and last editor from a live check, and a yes.
- **No silent overwrite.** Updates carry `--expected-version`; a newer version stops the run.
- **Nothing lost silently.** Each `WARN` is fixed in the source or named in the reply; rollback steps in HTML are rewritten, not dropped.
- **Images are listed by attachment name**, with any missing file or name clash called out before publishing.
- **Code survives byte for byte**, including a `]]>` inside it; the script checks the page is well-formed.
- **Tokens never appear** in a command, a file or the reply.
- **Facts untouched.** Restructuring Markdown never changes a command, threshold, name or date.

## Use something else when

- A Word file to edit with tracked changes; use `md-to-docx`
- Jira epics and issues from a PRD; use `tracker-brief-sync`
- Writing the runbook itself; use `runbook-generator`, then convert
